{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''William Thomas Trotter Jr.''' is an American mathematician, who is on the faculty of the Department of Mathematics at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]]. His main expertise is [[partially ordered set]]s, but he has also done significant work in other areas of [[combinatorics]],<ref>[http://www.math.gatech.edu/users/trotter Faculty profile], Georgia Institute of Technology, retrieved 2013-12-20.</ref> such as the [[Szemerédi–Trotter theorem]] and [[Chvátal-Rödl-Szemerédi-Trotter theorem]].

He completed his Ph.D. at the [[University of Alabama|University of Alabama-Tuscaloosa]] in 1969; his thesis, titled ''On Universal Subcontinua'', was written under the direction of William Jesse Gray.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=16440}}</ref> Trotter is the author of the book ''Combinatorics and partially ordered sets: dimension theory'' (Johns Hopkins University Press, 1992).<ref>{{citation|title=Review of ''Combinatorics and partially ordered sets''|journal=Mathematical Reviews|year=1994|mr=1169299|first=K. P.|last=Bogart}}</ref> With Mitchel Keller, he is also the author of a self-published textbook, ''Applied Combinatorics'' (2017).<ref>{{citation|url=https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/textbooks/applied-combinatorics|title=Applied Combinatorics|work=Open Textbook Library|year=2017 |publisher=University of Minnesota Center for Open Education}}</ref>
